statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-44171 is a path traversal in mbstream, the backup-archive extractor shipped with mariadb-backup: it did not reject '/../' in the file names inside an archive, so a crafted archive could make mbstream create files outside the target directory (GHSA-9pjh-5hhw-65v9, https://github.com/MariaDB/server/security/advisories/GHSA-9pjh-5hhw-65v9, MDEV-39408). MariaDB fixed it in 11.4.11 and 11.8.7, released on 18 May 2026, with commit https://github.com/MariaDB/server/commit/2bbfcb187602613611912238cbb765e6e7caed4b, which makes file_entry_new() in extra/mariabackup/xbstream.cc reject names that start with '.' or '/' or contain '/../' and print the message '%s: invalid filename %s'. Alpine records the fix at mariadb 11.4.11-r0 in its 3.23 security database (https://secdb.alpinelinux.org/v3.23/main.json). We checked the mariadb-backup package of every mariadb build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository as of 2026-11-28, 11.4.9-r0, 11.4.10-r0, 11.4.11-r0, 11.4.12-r0, 11.4.13-r0 and 11.4.14-r0, on x86_64 and aarch64: /usr/bin/mariadb-backup carries the MariaDB version string that matches its package version (11.4.9-MariaDB to 11.4.14-MariaDB), and /usr/bin/mbstream contains the fix's '%s: invalid filename %s' message in 11.4.11-r0 and every later build, and not in 11.4.9-r0 or 11.4.10-r0. 11.4.11-r0 is the first build with the fix, so the range ends there and the earlier builds are affected.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-44171 is a path traversal in mbstream, the backup-archive extractor shipped with mariadb-backup: it did not reject '/../' in the file names inside an archive, so a crafted archive could make mbstream create files outside the target directory (GHSA-9pjh-5hhw-65v9, https://github.com/MariaDB/server/security/advisories/GHSA-9pjh-5hhw-65v9, MDEV-39408). MariaDB fixed it in 11.4.11 and 11.8.7, released on 18 May 2026, with commit https://github.com/MariaDB/server/commit/2bbfcb187602613611912238cbb765e6e7caed4b, which makes file_entry_new() in extra/mariabackup/xbstream.cc reject names that start with '.' or '/' or contain '/../' and print the message '%s: invalid filename %s'. Debian fixes it in trixie with mariadb 1:11.8.8-0+deb13u1 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-44171). Every mariadb build published in the DHI Debian repository as of 2026-11-28 is one of four DHI rebuilds of Debian's mariadb 1:11.8.6-0+deb13u1, each with 56 binary packages per architecture including the -dbgsym packages, on amd64 and arm64. We checked the mariadb-backup package of all four builds on both architectures: /usr/bin/mariadb-backup reports MariaDB 11.8.6, /usr/bin/mbstream does not contain the fix's '%s: invalid filename %s' message, and the Debian changelog shipped in each build does not mention this CVE or MDEV-39408. Every published build is therefore affected until the owner ships MariaDB 11.8.7 or later, or a backport of the fix.
